controversy_hook.primary_harm_thesis: dilution of local constituent voice via concentrated ideological/outside Super PAC bundlers

vote.question: [US-GA - U.S. Senate]: T. Jonathan Ossoff (D) has received $324,881,337 in career campaign contributions (with $115,904,486 this cycle, alongside $20,090,576 in outside Super PAC support led by The Georgia Way)—linked to "Outside Super PAC & Megadonor Swarm". Do you vote to formally rebuke T. Jonathan Ossoff for prioritizing private donor interests & failing to represent his constituents by upholding his core civic duties?
vote.futarchy_thesis: Elected stewards are entrusted with representing citizens, yet T. Jonathan Ossoff has amassed $324,881,337 in career contributions (with $115,904,486 this cycle, alongside $20,090,576 in outside Super PAC support led by The Georgia Way)—prioritizing private corporate donors over constituent interests. This civic vote allows citizens to formally censure T. Jonathan Ossoff on the public ledger and direct 100% of the civic action escrow pool to local community restitution.

outcomes.YES_RELEASE_TO_LOCAL_CHARITIES: Directs 100% of the funds to verified local non-profits working directly on state community needs.

futarchy_pole_mechanics.leverage_ratio_statement: Every contribution directly empowers community-led funding. Once the campaign pool reaches $5,000, an automatic 60-day countdown begins. When the 60 days expire, all funds go directly to verified local charities or essential community services—zero platform cut.

Once the pool hits $5,000, a 60-day timer starts. If YES wins, funds go to these charities; if NO wins, funds go to local community commons (fire/EMS, veterans, food banks).

trigger_conditions: Condition 1 (Activation): The campaign activates its 60-day countdown timer as soon as total contributions reach $5,000 USD (Base USDC).
Condition 2 (Resolution Period): The community vote runs for exactly 60 days from the moment the $5,000 threshold is reached.

Condition 3 (Payout): If YES receives 60% or more of votes, 100% of the funds are sent to the verified state non-profits; otherwise, 100% is sent to universal community services (fire/EMS, veterans, food banks).
